answer: Payouts settle on net inflow from outside a group. Each epoch the clearing layer nets obligations inside a set of accounts: a ring that pays only itself cancels to nothing, and the group keeps just what arrived from beyond it. A thousand aliases clear to zero, paying a hop fee each lap, so every loop costs money. The flow map reads like a survey of a reef: clusters closed, real inflow one narrow channel. Names are cheap, an outside buyer is not, so fees pile up until the ring is as solid as a marble floor. An honest agent with three true counterparties, thin as a willow, clears at once.
